content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The bookmark-manager specification is ready for review.

- Spec: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- Quality checklist: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Validation: all 16 quality checks passed; no unresolved clarifications
- Scope: single-user web app with saving, editing, search, tags, favorites, archiving, sorting, and deletion
- Deferred: accounts, synchronization, sharing, import/export, browser extensions, and automatic page metadata

No plan or code has been created. Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll move to the implementation-plan gate.

Thanks for putting this together — I read through it, and a lot of it matches what I picture. Saving links, browsing them, editing, tags, favorites, archiving, search, sorting, deleting with a confirmation — that's all the right shape.

But a few things are off or missing from what I have in my head, and they matter to me:

1. **Typing in the title myself.** In your write-up I have to enter the title (and it's required). That's not what I want. When I paste in a web address, I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title, description, and its little icon for me automatically, so I mostly just paste and save. I still want to be able to fix or change any of that text afterward, but I shouldn't have to type it from scratch. You've got this listed as "out of scope," and I'd really like it in.

2. **A "read later" idea.** Favorites is fine, but separately I want to mark a link as something I still need to read, and then be able to pull up just those unread ones on their own. Marking it as read would take it off that list. I don't see that anywhere.

3. **Doing things to several bookmarks at once.** You've got bulk actions as out of scope. I'd want to be able to select a bunch of links and, say, tag them all, or archive them all, in one go — including everything currently showing after I've searched or filtered.

4. **Smarter searching.** Plain text search is good, but I also want to search by a tag specifically (something like typing `#news`), and to combine terms — this AND that, or one OR the other, and search an exact phrase in quotes. Also I'd want to filter by more than one tag at a time, not just one.

5. **When I save a link I already saved.** Your version lets me deliberately keep a second copy. I don't want duplicates at all — if the address is already there, I'd just want it to take me to the existing one to edit, not offer to make another copy.

A couple smaller things I'd also like eventually: writing a note in an link with basic formatting that shows nicely when I look at it, and saving a search-plus-tags combination so I can reuse it later. Those two are less urgent than the five above.

Could you revise the spec to bring those in? I'm not ready to approve it as written.

content:
The specification has been revised and revalidated.

Key decisions now captured:

- Automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval with graceful fallbacks
- Separate Read Later status and view
- Bulk actions across selected bookmarks or the complete filtered result set
- Advanced search with `#tags`, quoted phrases, `AND`, `OR`, and multi-tag filters
- Strict normalized-address duplicate prevention, opening the existing bookmark in edit mode
- Basic formatted notes
- Reusable named saved views
- New bookmarks default to read unless explicitly marked Read Later
- Multi-tag filters require all selected tags; alternatives can use `OR`

Review the revised artifacts:

- [Revised specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Validation: all 16 checks pass, with no unresolved clarifications

No planning or implementation has started. Please approve this revision or identify further changes before I move to the planning gate.

This looks great — you've picked up everything I asked about, and reading through it, it matches what I had in my head.

A few things I especially liked seeing spelled out: pasting an address and having the title, description, and icon come in on their own (with sensible fallbacks when a page won't cooperate), the separate Read Later list that stays independent from favorites, being able to select a whole filtered batch and act on it at once, searching by `#tag` and combining terms with AND/OR and exact phrases in quotes, and the app just taking me to the existing bookmark instead of ever making a duplicate. The formatted notes and the reusable saved searches are the nice-to-haves I mentioned, and I'm glad they're in too.

One small thing I want to confirm I understand, not a change: if I archive something I'd marked to read later, it disappears from my Read Later list while it's archived, but if I bring it back later it returns to Read Later as before — is that right? Your write-up reads that way to me and that's exactly what I'd want.

That's the only thing I wanted to check. Go ahead and move on to planning — the specification is approved.

content:
Bookmark Garden is complete and ready to review:

[Open the app at http://maker:4000/](http://maker:4000/)

Everything approved is implemented, including automatic metadata, duplicate prevention, Read Later/archive behavior, advanced search, formatted notes, bulk actions, permanent deletion, and saved views.

Validation passed:

- 256 unit, component, integration, and contract tests
- 10 complete browser journeys
- Accessibility and 320px responsive checks
- Search p95: ~180 ms
- 1,000-item bulk deletion p95: ~24 ms
- All 100 implementation tasks completed

Full evidence is in [validation.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/validation.md).

I had a good look and a proper play with it, and it does what I wanted.

The things I checked myself and was happy to see working for real:
- I pasted in a plain web address with nothing else, and it went and fetched the actual page's title on its own — it filled in "Example Domain" without me typing a thing. That's exactly the paste-and-save I was after.
- When I tried to save the same page again — even typing it slightly differently, with a trailing slash or different capital letters — it refused to make a second copy and pointed me straight back to the one I already had. That's the no-duplicates behavior I wanted.
- The layout has my Read Later list and Archive as their own separate places, favorites and reading filters kept apart, the smarter search with `#tag`, quotes and AND/OR right there with a little help link, the sorting choices, and a spot to save a search for reuse. Empty states read nicely too.

Between that and your write-up of everything you tested — the batch actions, formatted notes, the archive-and-restore-into-Read-Later behavior we confirmed earlier, and the saved views all being checked — I'm satisfied this is the app I asked for.

One thing I'll mention for down the road, not now: at some point I'd love a way to bring in bookmarks I've already got saved elsewhere, and to get mine back out. That's a future wish, not something I need before saying yes to this.

It's approved — thank you, this is lovely.
